item.title: Privacy advocates call on Maryland to investigate data brokers
item.description: Maryland has one of the strictest data privacy laws in the country. But privacy advocates allege that data brokers are violating the law by selling data to police and federal immigration agencies.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Open AI launches ChatGPT designed for younger users
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with CNBC's Ashley Capoot about OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens feature and the safety concerns it's designed to address.

item.title: Why tech companies are buying up tons of rare old books to train their AI models
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers speaks with 404 Media cofounder and reporter Emanuel Maiberg about his investigation into a shipment of rare books which ended up at an Amazon AI training warehouse.

item.title: Trump administration launches $5B AI initiative aimed at advancing science
item.description: The Trump administration has a new $5 billion initiative dedicated to using artificial intelligence to advance science. It's part of what the administration calls a new "golden age of science."

item.title: 'Profits won.' The child safety trial against Meta kicks off in federal court
item.description: Opening arguments are underway in a trial that pits four states against the company that owns Facebook and Instagram. They allege that Meta knew its products could hook kids — and lied about the danger.

item.title: Many recent grads say AI is making it harder to get a job. Economists aren't so sure
item.description: The unemployment rate for young adults with new degrees is higher than the rate for all workers, according to the New York Fed. Is AI the problem, or is it more complicated?

item.title: She told no one about her agony except ChatGPT. What her death reveals about AI risks
item.description: A 29-year-old woman confided her suicidal thoughts to an AI chatbot — not to her therapist, not to her parents, not to her best friend. What can AI learn from her death?
